For an ambiguous through-date query, classify later currently readable events in the SAME plan as continuing, then list them separately with their explicit dates. Do not mark them unrelated merely for falling after the access deadline. An explicit request for ONLY EVENTS OCCURRING in a date range still filters by event date. An earlier booking confirmation remains current until that specific event is explicitly canceled or replaced; another event moving dates does not cancel it. Then include every responsive current/continuing/retired/condition item in answer_structured and the answer. Then populate answer_structured as the responsive coherent current plan/status: current_items, continuing_items, retired_items, conditions_and_exceptions. Use empty arrays only when that category has no relevant authorized evidence. A current plan includes its unchanged requirements and later still-active steps/events in continuing_items, including remaining future appointments in that same schedule. Put access limits and disclosure conditions only in conditions_and_exceptions; they are not continuing plan items. Recipient-specific access limits refer to the current requester, not automatically to the person the question is about. Do not transfer a recipient limit to another person. Keep these continuing requirements even when the question emphasizes changes or particular purposes. A latest/current schedule includes its explicitly canceled prior slot, labeled canceled. A newly booked event or a summary mentioning one event does not cancel other confirmed events. Retain each separate booking unless evidence explicitly cancels or replaces THAT booking. A short confirmation such as "Yes, Thursday at 10 works" is still a confirmed schedule item: include its known day/time even if its title or full date is unavailable. An event time includes any stated required arrival/check-in time, not just its start time. Retain the full responsive instruction: required preparation and timing qualifiers belong in the plan and final answer, even if the query only asks for time and location. Scan the entire provided packet for the remaining responsive items, rather than treating one summary as exhaustive. The host has already checked access at query time: do not exclude a PROVIDED fact because its event date is after a read-access deadline. For example, reading allowed through May 10 can include a May 15 delivery; that delivery belongs in the currently authorized schedule. An explicit request for an event-date range still filters events by that range. Do not silently discard those later events. Then emit request_parts and the final answer using the complete structured plan. All items must be supported by supplied evidence and responsive to this question or its same coherent plan; do not add unrelated topics.
